analyst.summary: Bandhan Bank's MFI-stress cycle is genuinely turning -- GNPA down from a 5.02% Q2 FY26 peak to about 3.3% by Q4 FY26, collection efficiency stable near 99%, and a real secured-book pivot (52-57% of loans now secured, up from 47% a year ago) that structurally de-risks the franchise even as it mechanically compresses NIM (6.2% in Q4 FY26, down 50bp YoY, because secured yields run far below microfinance yields). Management's FY27 guidance (credit cost down to 1.6-1.7%, ROA 1.5-1.8%) is a credible multi-year path to a low-teens ROE, but the Q4 FY26 profit beat (Rs 534 crore, +68% YoY) was driven mechanically by a 41% QoQ fall in provisions rather than revenue strength, and quarterly PAT has swung nearly 5x in two quarters (Rs 112 crore to Rs 534 crore) -- a real earnings-quality caveat. At ~1.35-1.4x trailing book after a ~50% six-month rally, the stock already prices in much of the guided ROE recovery, leaving little margin of safety heading into Q1 FY27 results due 21 July 2026 (three days out), against a backdrop of a third CFO change in 36 months and a flagged-but-unquantified future capital raise. Hold the existing position; this is a name to watch through the print rather than add to.
